title: Battlecard No. 022 — Cornerstone (vocabulary collision on 'People Graph')
summary: On 2026-05-20 Cornerstone launched 'Cornerstone Workforce AI' with a trademark-noted Cornerstone People Graph, a Skills Engine, eleven-plus pre-built readiness agents (Proactive Coach, Embark Navigator, Future of Work, etc.), MCP integration into Slack and Microsoft Teams, and a direct Salesforce Agentforce / Data Cloud partnership. The substantive issue is not seat-by-seat competition — Cornerstone is L&D-anchored, not an MCP-native operating layer — but category-vocabulary capture: 'people graph' is becoming a category-level noun in 2026 HCM, and Cornerstone has staked an early claim with a 15-city Cornerstone Connect tour reinforcing the term through the year. Critical asymmetries on the AI side: Cornerstone did not name an LLM provider, did not publish an agent registry comparable to Workday ASOR, did not name a third-party bias auditor, did not ship a model card, and used the soft phrase 'certified AI guardrails' with no certifier specified. Recommendation is L3 Action Recommended with a 14-day window: (1) Forge or Yield publishes a depth-technical Stratum people-graph definition with architecture diagram, connector list, and explicit 'not an inference layer over our own data — a cross-system relational object built from yours' framing; (2) Compass adds a five-term vocabulary map (People Graph, Skills Engine, Agents, MCP, Workforce Readiness) to the buyer Q&A; (3) Helm articulates the 'operating layer vs readiness platform' frame so Stratum does not over-reach into Cornerstone's CLO umbrella. Battlecard No. 022 ships; competitors index updated to 22 cards live.
